question: According to Megasthenes, how many gates were there in Pataliputra?
solution:
The correct answer is __**64.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megasthenes** was a** Greek historian **who visited India during the** Mauryan Empire.**
 
• According to his accounts, **Pataliputra **was the capital city of the Mauryan Empire and had a total of** 64 gates.**
 
• These gates were made of **wood and iron **and were **heavily guarded** to protect the city from invaders.
 
• Megasthenes also mentioned that the city was surrounded by a** moat and a wooden wall.**
 
• Option 1, 2 and 3 are** incorrect **as they do not match with **Megasthenes' account** of the number of gates in Pataliputra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pataliputra was also known as **Patna** and is currently located in the **Indian state of Bihar.**
 
• The city was a major center of **trade, commerce** and **learning **during the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Option 1 (261) could be a reference to the **number of sub-cities **or wards within Pataliputra, as mentioned in some historical accounts.
 
• Option 2 (366) is** not supported** by any historical evidence and seems to be an arbitrary number.
 
• Option 3 (125) could be a reference to the **number of smaller gates or entrances** within the main gates of Pataliputra.
